To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FGF and BMP cooperate to regulate lens cell differentiation, that FGF induces a transient increase in BMP signaling, and that BMP inhibits FGF signaling in a negative feedback loop.

(1) BMP signaling is necessary for FGF-dependent lens cell differentiation; (2) the BMP signaling pathway can be activated by FGF in a manner independent of the canonical FGF receptor signaling pathway; and (3) FGF-dependent BMP signaling is necessary and sufficient to promote intercellular coupling in lens cells.

the FGF and BMP receptor signaling pathways cooperate in lens cells to regulate the expression of genes involved in lens cell differentiation and in the formation of gap junctional intercellular communication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BMP signaling in the regulation of cell proliferation and differentiation.
the molecular mechanisms of lens cell differentiation and how the lens is maintained as a functional tissue.
the role of BMP signaling in the lens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FGF and BMP synergistically regulate lens cell differentiation.
the FGF signaling pathway is a positive regulator of BMP signaling.

the FGF-BMP cross-talk is a positive interaction between these two pathways that is required for the maintenance of lens cell proliferation and the prevention of differentiation, and that this cross-talk is mediated through the Smad proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FGF pathway is required for BMP signaling to promote lens cell differentiation, and that BMP signaling is required for FGF signaling to promote lens fiber cell elongation and intercellular communication.
FGF and BMP synergistically regulate cell differentiation, intercellular coupling and the expression of cell-cell communication molecules in lens epithelial cells.
the FGF and BMP pathways synergize during lens cell differentiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGF and BMP can act synergistically in the lens to regulate cell proliferation and differentiation.
FGF and BMP ligands can cooperate to promote lens cell differentiation and that this cooperation requires the BMP receptor ALK6 (also known as activin-like kinase 6).
the FGF receptor (FGFR) is not only a negative regulator of BMP signaling, as previously described for epithelial cells, but also a positive regulator.
